annotations.title: Add a file to a fax

description: Use this when the person’s file is on their own disk, where you can run commands. Puts a PDF from the person’s own disk on their XipFax draft. A photo of any kind, such as a JPEG, PNG, HEIC, WebP, GIF or AVIF, goes as a PDF made from it first on their computer, upright as a photo viewer shows it: on a Mac, `sips -Z 2100 -s format pdf <photo> --out <name>.pdf` makes one, upright and at most 2,100 pixels on its long side. Any other kind of file, such as a Word file, goes once saved as a PDF. Work out the PDF’s size in bytes and its SHA-256 first, with a command such as `shasum -a 256 <file>`, and give both. The answer is an address good for 15 minutes and the headers to send with the file: PUT the file’s exact bytes there with each of those headers, such as with `curl --upload-file <file> -H "<name>: <value>" "<address>"`, then call finish_fax_file. The address takes this file alone. PDFs only, 40 MB at most.

name.description: Its name, such as its file’s: 255 characters at most.

sha256.description: Its SHA-256 in hex, 64 characters, as `shasum -a 256 <file>` prints it.

size_bytes.description: Its size in bytes: a PDF of 40 MB at most.

name: add_fax_file

name.description: Its name, as it was added.

page_count.description: Its pages, once XipFax has read it; null while it uploads.

status.description: `uploading` until XipFax has read it back, then `ready`. An open set: read what you know.

upload.description: Where the file goes: a PUT of its exact bytes to `url`, with each of these `headers`, within 15 minutes. It takes this one file and no other.
